subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE D&T simply, with an example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Mechanical advantage and changing force and motion

questions.q: Movement in a straight line in one direction is best described as which type of motion?
questions.explain: Linear motion is movement in a straight line in a single direction, e.g. a train moving along a straight track.

questions.q: The needle of a sewing machine moves up and down repeatedly in a straight line. Which type of motion is this?
questions.explain: Reciprocating motion is repeated backwards-and-forwards (or up-and-down) movement in a straight line, exactly like a sewing-machine needle.

questions.q: A pendulum swinging back and forth about a fixed pivot is an example of which type of motion?
questions.explain: Oscillating motion is swinging backwards and forwards along a curved path about a pivot, as with a pendulum. Reciprocating is in a straight line, not curved.

questions.q: The wheel of a car turning about its axle is an example of which type of motion?
questions.explain: Rotary motion is movement in a circle around a fixed point or axis, such as a wheel spinning on its axle.

questions.q: In a first-class lever, what is the correct arrangement of the three parts?
options: The load is between the fulcrum and the effort
The effort is between the fulcrum and the load
The fulcrum is between the effort and the load
Load and effort on the same side of the fulcrum
questions.explain: In a first-class lever the fulcrum (pivot) sits between the effort and the load, e.g. a see-saw or a pair of scissors.

questions.q: A wheelbarrow has the load between the effort (handles) and the fulcrum (wheel). Which class of lever is this?
questions.explain: A second-class lever has the load positioned between the fulcrum and the effort, as in a wheelbarrow or nutcracker.

questions.q: Fishing rods and tweezers, where the effort is between the fulcrum and the load, are examples of which class of lever?
questions.explain: A third-class lever has the effort between the fulcrum and the load. This gives a larger, faster output movement but no mechanical advantage in force, as with tweezers.

questions.q: A reverse-motion linkage is used to...
options: Change rotary motion into reciprocating motion
Make an output move in the opposite direction to the input
Keep two levers moving in parallel
Increase the size of an output force
questions.explain: A reverse-motion linkage has a single fixed pivot in the middle so the output moves in the opposite direction to the input.

questions.q: A bell-crank linkage is most useful because it can...
options: Convert rotary motion to linear motion
Reverse the speed of a gear train
Double the input force with no change of direction
Change the direction of a force through 90 degrees
questions.explain: A bell-crank is an L-shaped linkage pivoted at the corner; it changes the direction of a force through roughly 90 degrees, e.g. bicycle brakes.

questions.q: A designer needs the output arm of a mechanism to move up and down while staying horizontal (like a parallelogram). Which linkage should be used?
questions.explain: A parallel-motion (parallelogram) linkage keeps the output moving parallel to the input, e.g. an anglepoise lamp or toolbox tray.

questions.q: In a cam-and-follower mechanism, what conversion of motion takes place?
options: Rotary motion into rotary motion at a different speed
questions.explain: As the cam rotates, the follower rides on its profile and moves up and down, converting rotary input into reciprocating output.

questions.q: The maximum distance a follower rises and falls as a cam rotates is known as the...
questions.explain: The stroke (or lift) is the total vertical distance the follower moves. A 'dwell' is the period when the follower stays still.

questions.q: A driver gear has 20 teeth and the driven gear has 60 teeth. What is the gear ratio (driven : driver)?
questions.explain: Gear ratio = teeth on driven / teeth on driver = 60 / 20 = 3, giving 3 : 1. The larger driven gear turns more slowly with more torque.

questions.q: A driver gear with 40 teeth meshes with a driven gear with 10 teeth. If the driver turns at 100 rpm, how fast does the driven gear turn?
questions.explain: Output speed = input speed x (driver teeth / driven teeth) = 100 x (40/10) = 400 rpm. The smaller driven gear spins faster.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of adding an idler gear between a driver and a driven gear?
options: To reverse the driven gear so it turns the same way as the driver
To convert rotary motion into linear motion
To change the overall gear ratio
questions.explain: An idler gear does not change the overall gear ratio; it simply makes the driven gear rotate in the same direction as the driver.

questions.q: A driver pulley of diameter 50 mm drives a larger pulley of diameter 100 mm by a belt. What is the velocity ratio (driven : driver)?
questions.explain: Velocity ratio = driven diameter / driver diameter = 100 / 50 = 2, i.e. 2 : 1. The larger driven pulley turns at half the speed of the driver.

questions.q: Compared with a pulley-and-belt drive, a key advantage of a sprocket-and-chain drive (as on a bicycle) is that it...
options: Is quieter and needs no lubrication
Automatically reverses the direction of rotation
Cannot slip, so it transmits drive positively
Can transmit motion between shafts that are far apart only
questions.explain: The chain engages positively with the teeth of the sprockets so it cannot slip, unlike a belt which can slip under load.

questions.q: If two pulleys are connected by a belt that is NOT crossed, the two pulleys will...
options: Always rotate at the same speed
questions.explain: An open (uncrossed) belt makes both pulleys turn in the same direction. Crossing the belt reverses the driven pulley's direction.

questions.lo: Mechanical advantage and changing force and motion
questions.q: A lever is used to lift a load of 600 N with an effort of 150 N. What is the mechanical advantage?
questions.explain: Mechanical advantage = load / effort = 600 / 150 = 4. An MA greater than 1 means the effort is multiplied to move a larger load.

questions.lo: Mechanical advantage and changing force and motion
questions.q: A mechanism with a mechanical advantage of less than 1 will...
options: Give a larger, faster output movement but a smaller output force
Reverse the direction of the load
Have no effect on speed or force
questions.explain: When MA is less than 1 the output force is smaller than the effort, but the trade-off is a greater range/speed of movement, as in a third-class lever.
